title: Dickson's conjecture versus superadditivity of prime-constellation counts: explicit certificates, the exact twin-prime crossing, and a registry of incompatible conjectures
abstract: Hensley and Richards (1974) showed that the prime k-tuples conjecture contradicts the Hardy-Littlewood inequality pi(x+y) <= pi(x)+pi(y). This note records the same incompatibility for constellation counting functions (twin primes, cousins, sexy primes, two triplet patterns, quadruplets) with small explicit certificates verified by a few lines of code; for twin primes the crossing occurs already at window length 396 (22 admissible twin-pair positions of diameter 392 versus pi_2(396)=21), and each conditional statement is checked to be non-vacuous by an exhaustive scan of the actual primes. A self-contained certificate for the original Hensley-Richards incompatibility (an admissible 1699-tuple of diameter below 14500 versus pi(14500)=1698) is included, together with an explicit remote window, built by the Chinese remainder theorem, containing 1699 integers free of prime factors up to 1699. This refutes unconditionally the central claim of a recent preprint (Zenodo record 21896925) that remote intervals can never have prime capacity exceeding pi(y); that preprint's Theorem 1 is also shown to fail for every window length y from 2 to 2000. Computations, certificates and text were prepared with the assistance of an AI system (Claude, Anthropic); the author is responsible for the content. Version 4 adds the incompatibility-graph registry as supplementary data: edges.json (120 proven edges of the form 'A and B cannot both hold', each with mechanism, source and status: 33 certificate edges, 79 literature edges across number theory, fine-grained and structural complexity, harmonic analysis, arithmetic geometry and set theory, 8 trivial), nodes.json (believed/refuted statuses), registry.md (table), graph.html (interactive rendering) and build.py; plus 22 further certificate systems from an automated pipeline (constellations, Cunningham chains, arithmetic progressions, quadratic and cubic polynomials). Version 4.1: graph.html rebuilt as a standalone English page (UTF-8 declared; the previous file lacked a charset declaration and rendered garbled outside a hosting wrapper) with a corrected force layout. Version 5: the registry grows to 1096 edges (959 certificate edges from an automated pipeline over 987 systems: prime pairs {0,2k} up to k=60, all admissible even triples of diameter <= 40 and quadruples of diameter <= 30, arithmetic progressions a mod q for q <= 40, quadratic polynomials n^2+c and n^2+n+c; 124 literature edges; 13 trivial). Certificate edges compared against an initial segment with at most two occurrences are tagged 'HR-thin'. All certificate edges share one mechanism and count once as evidence; the tags allow restricting the graph to edges between independently held conjectures. Version 6: (i) the exact twin-prime crossing: the least window length at which an admissible configuration of twin-pair positions beats the initial segment is y0 = 379 (theorem, with the table of minimal diameters D(K) of admissible K-packings of twin pairs for K <= 23, program supplied, independently recomputed); (ii) ten composite incompatibilities between named statements with proofs and prior-art status (five published in substance, four folklore, one -- Chang's conjecture versus Diamond-plus -- not found stated); (iii) the registry grows to 268 edges between named conjectures (1268 edges in total), most of the new ones found by literature-search agents and confirmed by adversarial verifier agents; the full verifier log is supplied. Version 7: registry data update only; 349 edges between named conjectures (1349 in total) after three rounds of agent search and adversarial verification across ten domains; both verifier logs supplied.

title: Formal Specification of PLOS (Principle Language Operating System): A Semantic Integration OS for Structural Coherence Across Heterogeneous Systems
abstract: This paper formalizes PLOS (Principle Language Operating System) as the semantic integration layer within the Meta‑OS architecture. PLOS provides meaning‑level synchronization, cross‑domain semantic resolution, and contextual coherence—capabilities that AI models cannot achieve. Building upon AI Performance Contribution in Three Layers: Convergence Speed, Precision Adaptability, and Structural Coherence — Insights from 250,000 Claude Conversations, this work defines the formal semantics, invariants, and interface architecture required for deterministic semantic behavior across heterogeneous systems. PLOS ensures that meaning remains stable, coherent, and aligned with long‑range principles, enabling coherent operation in industrial, societal, and autonomous domains. It represents the first formalized Semantic OS, bridging the gap between data‑level consistency and structural‑level coherence in AI‑integrated societies.

title: L'EFFICACITÉ SYMBOLIQUE DE L'ARACHIDE "MUTSHIETU" DANS LA CULTURE SUKU : APPROCHE ETHNO-ANTHROPOLOGIQUE DANS LES SECTEURS DE LOBO ET GANAKETI, TERRITOIRE DE FESHI, RDC
abstract: Cette étude analyse l’efficacité symbolique attribuée à l’arachide « Mutshietu » dans la culture Suku, à partir des représentations et des pratiques observées dans les secteurs de Lobo et de Ganaketi, territoire de Feshi, dans la province du Kwango en République démocratique du Congo. Alors que les approches agronomiques et nutritionnelles tendent principalement à considérer l’arachide sous l’angle de sa valeur alimentaire, cette recherche s’intéresse à ses dimensions sociales, thérapeutiques, éthiques, cognitives et symboliques. Elle s’inscrit dans une approche ethno-anthropologique fondée sur des entretiens semi-directifs réalisés en 2023 et 2024 auprès de 25 informateurs, dont 15 chefs de clans et 10 femmes cultivatrices Suku. L’analyse mobilise principalement les concepts d’efficacité symbolique de Claude Lévi-Strauss, de classification et de tabou alimentaire de Mary Douglas, ainsi que celui de force vitale développé par Placide Tempels. Les résultats mettent en évidence cinq principaux registres d’efficacité symbolique attribués à Mutshietu : social, thérapeutique, éthique, cognitif et vital. L’arachide apparaît notamment comme un support de réconciliation et de cohésion sociale, de transmission des savoirs et des normes, ainsi que comme un élément participant aux représentations relatives à la santé, à la fertilité, à l’abondance et aux relations entre les vivants, la terre et les ancêtres. L’étude montre ainsi que Mutshietu constitue un élément important du patrimoine culturel Suku, dont la disparition progressive pourrait entraîner la perte de pratiques, de savoirs et de significations sociales qui lui sont associés. Elle recommande, en conséquence, une meilleure prise en compte des dimensions culturelles des aliments traditionnels dans les politiques de conservation des ressources locales, de développement rural et de valorisation des savoirs endogènes.

title: Meta‑OS: A Four‑Layer Structural Operating System for Coherence, Integration, and Cross‑Domain Synchronization
abstract: This specification defines Meta‑OS, a four‑layer structural operating system designed to maintain coherence across heterogeneous physical, data, semantic, and value systems. Building upon AI Performance Contribution in Three Layers: Convergence Speed, Precision Adaptability, and Structural Coherence — Insights from 250,000 Claude Conversations, Meta‑OS provides the structural coherence that AI models cannot achieve. Its architecture consists of four deterministic layers—Physical Synchronization, Data Integration, Semantic Integration (PLOS), and Structural Coherence—each enforcing invariants and participating in cross‑layer synchronization protocols. Meta‑OS ensures long‑range consistency, multi‑objective alignment, and deterministic propagation across industrial, societal, and autonomous systems. It represents the first complete Structural OS capable of supporting AI‑integrated societies, providing the coherence required for resilient, scalable, and principled multi‑domain systems.

title: Dickson's conjecture versus superadditivity of prime-constellation counts: explicit certificates, the exact twin-prime crossing, and a registry of incompatible conjectures
abstract: Hensley and Richards (1974) showed that the prime k-tuples conjecture contradicts the Hardy-Littlewood inequality pi(x+y) <= pi(x)+pi(y). This note records the same incompatibility for constellation counting functions (twin primes, cousins, sexy primes, two triplet patterns, quadruplets) with small explicit certificates verified by a few lines of code; for twin primes the crossing occurs already at window length 396 (22 admissible twin-pair positions of diameter 392 versus pi_2(396)=21), and each conditional statement is checked to be non-vacuous by an exhaustive scan of the actual primes. A self-contained certificate for the original Hensley-Richards incompatibility (an admissible 1699-tuple of diameter below 14500 versus pi(14500)=1698) is included, together with an explicit remote window, built by the Chinese remainder theorem, containing 1699 integers free of prime factors up to 1699. This refutes unconditionally the central claim of a recent preprint (Zenodo record 21896925) that remote intervals can never have prime capacity exceeding pi(y); that preprint's Theorem 1 is also shown to fail for every window length y from 2 to 2000. Computations, certificates and text were prepared with the assistance of an AI system (Claude, Anthropic); the author is responsible for the content. Version 4 adds the incompatibility-graph registry as supplementary data: edges.json (120 proven edges of the form 'A and B cannot both hold', each with mechanism, source and status: 33 certificate edges, 79 literature edges across number theory, fine-grained and structural complexity, harmonic analysis, arithmetic geometry and set theory, 8 trivial), nodes.json (believed/refuted statuses), registry.md (table), graph.html (interactive rendering) and build.py; plus 22 further certificate systems from an automated pipeline (constellations, Cunningham chains, arithmetic progressions, quadratic and cubic polynomials). Version 4.1: graph.html rebuilt as a standalone English page (UTF-8 declared; the previous file lacked a charset declaration and rendered garbled outside a hosting wrapper) with a corrected force layout. Version 5: the registry grows to 1096 edges (959 certificate edges from an automated pipeline over 987 systems: prime pairs {0,2k} up to k=60, all admissible even triples of diameter <= 40 and quadruples of diameter <= 30, arithmetic progressions a mod q for q <= 40, quadratic polynomials n^2+c and n^2+n+c; 124 literature edges; 13 trivial). Certificate edges compared against an initial segment with at most two occurrences are tagged 'HR-thin'. All certificate edges share one mechanism and count once as evidence; the tags allow restricting the graph to edges between independently held conjectures. Version 6: (i) the exact twin-prime crossing: the least window length at which an admissible configuration of twin-pair positions beats the initial segment is y0 = 379 (theorem, with the table of minimal diameters D(K) of admissible K-packings of twin pairs for K <= 23, program supplied, independently recomputed); (ii) ten composite incompatibilities between named statements with proofs and prior-art status (five published in substance, four folklore, one -- Chang's conjecture versus Diamond-plus -- not found stated); (iii) the registry grows to 268 edges between named conjectures (1268 edges in total), most of the new ones found by literature-search agents and confirmed by adversarial verifier agents; the full verifier log is supplied. Version 7: registry data update only; 349 edges between named conjectures (1349 in total) after three rounds of agent search and adversarial verification across ten domains; both verifier logs supplied.

title: L'EFFICACITÉ SYMBOLIQUE DE L'ARACHIDE "MUTSHIETU" DANS LA CULTURE SUKU : APPROCHE ETHNO-ANTHROPOLOGIQUE DANS LES SECTEURS DE LOBO ET GANAKETI, TERRITOIRE DE FESHI, RDC
abstract: Cette étude analyse l’efficacité symbolique attribuée à l’arachide « Mutshietu » dans la culture Suku, à partir des représentations et des pratiques observées dans les secteurs de Lobo et de Ganaketi, territoire de Feshi, dans la province du Kwango en République démocratique du Congo. Alors que les approches agronomiques et nutritionnelles tendent principalement à considérer l’arachide sous l’angle de sa valeur alimentaire, cette recherche s’intéresse à ses dimensions sociales, thérapeutiques, éthiques, cognitives et symboliques. Elle s’inscrit dans une approche ethno-anthropologique fondée sur des entretiens semi-directifs réalisés en 2023 et 2024 auprès de 25 informateurs, dont 15 chefs de clans et 10 femmes cultivatrices Suku. L’analyse mobilise principalement les concepts d’efficacité symbolique de Claude Lévi-Strauss, de classification et de tabou alimentaire de Mary Douglas, ainsi que celui de force vitale développé par Placide Tempels. Les résultats mettent en évidence cinq principaux registres d’efficacité symbolique attribués à Mutshietu : social, thérapeutique, éthique, cognitif et vital. L’arachide apparaît notamment comme un support de réconciliation et de cohésion sociale, de transmission des savoirs et des normes, ainsi que comme un élément participant aux représentations relatives à la santé, à la fertilité, à l’abondance et aux relations entre les vivants, la terre et les ancêtres. L’étude montre ainsi que Mutshietu constitue un élément important du patrimoine culturel Suku, dont la disparition progressive pourrait entraîner la perte de pratiques, de savoirs et de significations sociales qui lui sont associés. Elle recommande, en conséquence, une meilleure prise en compte des dimensions culturelles des aliments traditionnels dans les politiques de conservation des ressources locales, de développement rural et de valorisation des savoirs endogènes.

title: Formal Specification of PLOS (Principle Language Operating System): A Semantic Integration OS for Structural Coherence Across Heterogeneous Systems
abstract: This paper formalizes PLOS (Principle Language Operating System) as the semantic integration layer within the Meta‑OS architecture. PLOS provides meaning‑level synchronization, cross‑domain semantic resolution, and contextual coherence—capabilities that AI models cannot achieve. Building upon AI Performance Contribution in Three Layers: Convergence Speed, Precision Adaptability, and Structural Coherence — Insights from 250,000 Claude Conversations, this work defines the formal semantics, invariants, and interface architecture required for deterministic semantic behavior across heterogeneous systems. PLOS ensures that meaning remains stable, coherent, and aligned with long‑range principles, enabling coherent operation in industrial, societal, and autonomous domains. It represents the first formalized Semantic OS, bridging the gap between data‑level consistency and structural‑level coherence in AI‑integrated societies.

title: Meta‑OS: A Four‑Layer Structural Operating System for Coherence, Integration, and Cross‑Domain Synchronization
abstract: This specification defines Meta‑OS, a four‑layer structural operating system designed to maintain coherence across heterogeneous physical, data, semantic, and value systems. Building upon AI Performance Contribution in Three Layers: Convergence Speed, Precision Adaptability, and Structural Coherence — Insights from 250,000 Claude Conversations, Meta‑OS provides the structural coherence that AI models cannot achieve. Its architecture consists of four deterministic layers—Physical Synchronization, Data Integration, Semantic Integration (PLOS), and Structural Coherence—each enforcing invariants and participating in cross‑layer synchronization protocols. Meta‑OS ensures long‑range consistency, multi‑objective alignment, and deterministic propagation across industrial, societal, and autonomous systems. It represents the first complete Structural OS capable of supporting AI‑integrated societies, providing the coherence required for resilient, scalable, and principled multi‑domain systems.
